subject: BrightHold POC: scope, SLOs & next-step checklist
messages:
----- Message 1 -----
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference>
To: Amit Rao <amit@brighthold.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: BrightHold POC: scope, SLOs & next-step checklist

Hi Amit / Elena —

Great conversation this morning. Thanks for walking through BrightHold's primary goals for this POC; below is a concise recap and a proposed success checklist so we can align expectations before we kick off. Please reply with any edits and confirm you can start the trial on 4/19.

Quick recap of BrightHold goals (from discovery):
- Improve QA/triage automation for support tickets (reduce manual review by >40%)
- Surface suggested responses with <600ms median latency at 250 QPS for peak slicing
- Keep per-token inference cost below $0.0015 in steady-state
- Maintain top-line precision/acceptability rate >= 87% on sampled production prompts

Proposed POC scope and timeline:
- Duration: 3 weeks (4/19 -> 5/9) with a mid-point readout week of 4/30
- Workloads: sample corpus (up to 50k historical tickets) + 3 live test routes
- Owners: BrightHold engineering (ingest + validation), Redwood SRE/SE (serving, SLO verification)

Success criteria (objective KPIs):
1) Latency: median generation latency <= 600ms across the 90th percentile of sample routes; P95 under 900ms.
2) Throughput: sustain 250 qps for 1-minute windows with <5% tail latency spikes.
3) Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0015 for inference when using recommended batching/quantization.
4) Quality: human-evaluated acceptability >= 87% on a blinded sample of 300 outputs (3 reviewers)

Technical ask list (prior to kickoff):
- BrightHold: share a de-identified sample corpus (S3 or Drive) and a short list of high-priority prompts (by 4/15)
- Redwood: provide POC runbook, test harness, and metric dashboard (attached)
- Both: finalize NDA/contract signature (DocuSign link below)

Attachments: redwood-poc-outline.pdf (POC plan), sample-metrics-template.xlsx (metric capture template)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/NDA-sign-BH-042
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/BH-2027-042

Next steps (action items):
- Amit: confirm sample corpus availability and the requested start date (4/19) — due 4/15
- Redwood (Jasmine/Ben): prepare environment and provide SRE contact for run-of trial — target 4/16
- Marissa: review and approve any trial commercial adjustments (if BrightHold requests extended testing)

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0133

----- Message 2 -----
From: Amit Rao <amit@brighthold.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@brighthold.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightHold POC: scope, SLOs & next-step checklist

Jasmine —

Thanks for the detailed recap. This aligns well. A few clarifications from our side:
1) Corpus: we can share 40k de-identified tickets via an S3 bucket by 4/15.
2) Latency target: 600ms median is ambitious for our longer threads (>=800 tokens). Can we scope the 600ms target to the most common route (short responses) and set a separate P95 target for long-form suggestions?
3) Cost: we're comfortable with $0.0015/token as a benchmarking target, but can you provide a run-rate estimate based on our expected ~2M tokens/day if scaled?

We can confirm start on 4/19 provided we get the trial runbook and a contact for Redwood's SRE. Also we'd like a quick sync between our infra lead and Ben to confirm integration details — Elena and I are available Wed 4/14 in the afternoon PST.

– Amit
Prospect: BrightHold AI

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: BrightHold POC: scope, SLOs & next-step checklist

Amit / Jasmine —

Thanks — echoing the plan and adding a technical checklist so we don't miss the gating items on day 1.
Day-0 technical checklist:
- Provide S3 path and IAM read role for the de-identified corpus (we'll only pull the agreed bucket)
- Share a traffic profile (QPS over 24h) and representative prompt length distribution (so we can pre-select kernel/quantization config)
- Confirm whether the 3 live test routes require stateful context across calls (conversation threads) or are single-shot

POC validation approach (how we'll measure):
- Latency: run synthetic replay of your traffic mix in our sandbox; report median/P95/P99 across buckets and compare to live wire tests
- Throughput: ramp test to 250 qps sustained for 1 minute; if failure, we iterate on batching and routing policy to meet target
- Cost: we will capture per-token costing with the recommended batching/quant profile and provide a simulated 2M tokens/day run-rate estimate (benches attached)
- Quality: blind human eval on 300 samples; we'll supply the rubric and help recruit reviewers if needed

Quick asks for your infra lead call on 4/14:
- Elena: can you confirm whether you have any egress restrictions or VPC peering needs?
- Also: do you require our private deployment option for the POC, or will hosted be sufficient for the initial run? Hosted is faster to spin up; private requires a short network handoff.

I'll be on the 4/14 sync and can run the demo of the replay harness.

Attachment: sample-metrics-template.xlsx

Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference | +1 (650) 555-0199

Team —

This reads well. A few internal notes:
- Jasmine: confirm the commercial baseline (trial credits + any discount if trial extends). If they need extended testing beyond 3 weeks, keep the ask for central approval.
- Ben: please include a short security checklist in the runbook (SOC2 controls we will verify; opt-out for private deployment if they want hosted).
- Grace: please own the mid-point readout slides (4/30) and coordinate with BrightHold on reviewers.

Amit / Elena — happy to have your infra leads meet with Ben on 4/14. Once we have the sample corpus and IAM read access, Redwood will provision the sandbox and send the runbook steps.
